h: Sacred Eating Makes the Heart Worthy of Its Requests

p: And in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 61b):
who eat food…" and so on,
"from a supernal place, precious above all,
"wisdom gives life to those who possess it" (Koheles 7:12).
And it is superior to manna.
are those who toil in Torah,
that are distinguished in halachah…" and so on;
every one of Yisrael is distinguished in halachah,
since he fulfills a matter of halachah,
in that he rests from labor;
and "one who sat and did not commit a sin…" and so on,
"is like one who performs a mitzvah" (Kiddushin 39b);
"a matter of sin came to his hand
and he was saved from it,"
since he is accustomed to labor
in the aspect of talmidei chachamim,
"Are you more important to us than it?"
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (יוֹמָא לט, א)
in the manner of what they said (Yoma 39a):
no Kiddush at all is said,
only the blessing Borei pri hagafen;
וּבַזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ, חֵלֶק ג קעג, א)
And in the holy Zohar (on this parshah, Zohar III 173a):
this is washing of the hands";
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת נג, ב)
and this is according to what they said (Berachos 53b):
"'And from Tzion may He sustain you':
that is, in that a person recognizes
is the One who brings forth bread,
and He is the One who feeds;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁבִּיקֵּשׁ יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם (בְּרֵאשִׁית כח, כ)
as Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him, asked (Bereishis 28:20):
"And He will give me bread to eat":
that He should be the One who gives,
and He should be the One who feeds;
"'May He remember all your meal offerings':
'all' is to include…" and so on;
"this is the final washing of the hands";
this is the blessing of zimmun."
That is, through the final waters
it comes about that the eating is
like meal offerings and burnt offerings.
And as is written in the Gemara (there):
for the term "and you shall be" implies
and spoke words of Torah over it,
it is as though they ate
from the table of the Omnipresent,
This is the table that is before Hashem."
And this pasuk was said of the altar,
'May He grant you according to your heart…'"
That is, in that same psalm
and it is stated in Midrash Tehillim (20:5)
that is not prayed for every person,
יֵשׁ בְּלִבּוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם לִגְנוֹב וְכוּלֵּי
a person has it in his heart to steal…" and so on;
it was prayed for him thus."
And as we find in the Tanchuma (Terumah 9):
do not give him…" and so on.
one should not pray for him,
But because his heart is whole,
and it is known that he will desire
it was prayed for him thus.
And the main wholeness of the heart
as is written in the Midrash
that delicacies not enter his body";
and similarly in Tanna d'Vei Eliyahu
that it not enter his innards…" and so on;
for the main beginning of the serpent's enticement
was through bodily pleasure in eating.
and it does not say which heart.
Only, when the eating is for bodily pleasure,
מִתְגַּבֵּר עַל יְדֵי זֶה הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע
the yetzer hara grows strong through it,
"the heart of the fool, on his left";
and when the eating is in holiness,
then his heart is whole before his Creator,
and he has but one heart
"May He grant you according to your heart"
and similarly to what they expounded (Bereishis Rabbah 48:11):
וְסַעֲדוּ לְבַבְכֶם אֵין כְּתִיב כָּאן וְכוּלֵּי
"'And sustain your heart': 'your hearts' is not written here…" and so on.
הוּא עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין כו, ב)
this is according to what they said (Sanhedrin 26b):
עֲצַת ה׳ הִיא תָקוּם (מִשְׁלֵי יט, כא)
"'the counsel of Hashem, it shall stand' (Mishlei 19:21):
counsel in which there is the word of Hashem,
And when the eating is in holiness,
then in all his deeds and thoughts
he is for its own sake,
in which there is the word of Hashem,
since his heart is whole before his Creator.
that is, on Shabbos there is effective
into the eating and drinking of Yisrael,
since the holiness comes from Hashem Yisbarach,
And as a matter of course his heart also becomes
And this is what the Gemara says (Shabbos 118b):
is given the requests of his heart,
and He will give you the requests of your heart';
That is, through the eating of Shabbos
כָּל מִשְׁאֲלוֹת לִבּוֹ שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל לְטוֹבָה
all the requests of a Jew's heart are for good,
for his heart is whole before his Creator.
And this is "His light will dwell upon it":
that comes from Hashem Yisbarach from above,
